verdict.summary: Exceptionally strong post-MPNU cash generation: 9M26 Adj EBITDA jumped 38% YoY to $1,530m and FCF hit $749m, slashing net debt 65% to $234.9m (0.14x Net Leverage). On 27-Oct-26 Seplat cleared the final $100m MPNU acquisition facility, leaving the $650m 9.125% 2030 Eurobond as the primary debt instrument against $556.9m cash. Sovereign ceiling (B/B2/B) and shareholder payout increases (Q3 div +58% to 19c/sh) are key watch items.

positives: Ultra-low leverage: Net debt cut 65% from $673.3m (FY25) to $234.9m at 30-Sep-26 (0.14x Net Debt/EBITDA), with $556.9m cash.
Zero acquisition debt overhang: Final $100m MPNU acquisition facility repaid on 27-Oct-26; 2026 7.75% notes refinanced into 2030s.
Scale & offshore diversification: 9M26 production averaged 145kboepd (Q3: 155.8kboepd) with $8-10/bbl premium pricing over Brent.
negatives: Nigeria sovereign ceiling (S&P B, Moody's B2, Fitch B) caps ratings despite near-net-cash balance sheet.
Rising shareholder distributions: Q3 dividend lifted 58% QoQ to 19.0c/share (core 5c + special 14c).
Oil price sensitivity & Nigerian onshore pipeline/regulatory operating risks.

background.business_overview: Leading Nigerian independent oil and gas producer operating onshore OMLs, shallow-water offshore MPNU assets, and ANOH gas processing.
background.asset_perimeter: Consolidated Nigerian onshore + MPNU shallow-water offshore E&P; dual-listed LSE & NGX.
background.ownership_governance: Independent public E&P listed in London and Lagos; strong international bond market track record.
